days.title: Day 1 – Advanced CSS Architecture & Methodologies
days.definition: Comprehensive approaches for organizing and scaling CSS in large-scale applications using methodologies like BEM, SMACSS, OOCSS, ITCSS, and utility-first frameworks.

explanation.main: CSS methodologies provide systematic, scalable approaches for maintainable codebases in enterprise applications.
key_points: BEM (Block, Element, Modifier) deep dive with complex component patterns
SMACSS (Scalable Modular Architecture) with five-layer categorization
OOCSS (Object-Oriented) separating structure from skin and container from content
ITCSS (Inverted Triangle) with 7 layers for controlled specificity
Atomic Design methodology for design systems
Utility-first CSS with functional class patterns
CSS-in-JS comparison: Styled-components vs Emotion vs Stitches

quiz.question: What is the correct order of ITCSS layers from low to high specificity?
options: Settings → Tools → Generic → Elements → Objects → Components → Utilities
Utilities → Components → Objects → Elements → Generic → Tools → Settings
Generic → Elements → Objects → Components → Utilities → Settings → Tools
Settings → Generic → Tools → Elements → Objects → Components → Utilities
quiz.answer: Settings → Tools → Generic → Elements → Objects → Components → Utilities
quiz.reasoning: ITCSS uses an inverted triangle where layers progress from low specificity (settings) to high specificity (utilities).

quiz.question: In Atomic Design, what represents a group of molecules working together?
quiz.reasoning: Atomic Design hierarchy: Atoms (basic elements) → Molecules (groups of atoms) → Organisms (groups of molecules) → Templates → Pages.

quiz.question: What is the main advantage of utility-first CSS?
quiz.reasoning: Utility-first CSS provides pre-defined classes for rapid development and ensures design consistency across projects.

explanation.main: Mastering CSS performance leads to faster load times, smoother interactions, and better user engagement metrics.
key_points: Critical CSS extraction and implementation strategies
CSS loading optimization: preload, prefetch, lazy loading
GPU accelerated properties and will-change optimization
CSS containment and rendering layer management
Animation performance: requestAnimationFrame vs CSS animations
Performance auditing tools: Lighthouse, WebPageTest, CSS Stats
Bundle splitting and code delivery optimization

quiz.question: Which CSS properties trigger the cheapest rendering operations?
quiz.reasoning: transform and opacity can be handled by the compositor thread without triggering layout or paint operations.

quiz.question: What does the 'contain' CSS property improve?
quiz.reasoning: The contain property creates a containment context, preventing layout/paint calculations from affecting outside elements.

quiz.question: When should you use will-change property?
options: Only when animation performance issues occur
On elements that will definitely change soon
quiz.answer: On elements that will definitely change soon
quiz.reasoning: will-change should be applied sparingly to elements that will actually change, as it consumes memory resources.

days.title: Day 3 – Advanced Responsive & Adaptive Design
days.definition: Modern responsive design techniques beyond media queries, including container queries, intrinsic design, fluid typography, responsive images, and adaptive components.

explanation.main: Contemporary responsive design adapts to both viewport and container contexts using CSS's latest features.
key_points: Container queries and @container rule with size and style conditions
Intrinsic design: min(), max(), clamp() functions for fluid layouts
Fluid typography and spacing with viewport units and calculations
Responsive images: srcset, sizes, picture element, and art direction
Aspect-ratio property and intrinsic sizing
Viewport-relative units: vw, vh, vmin, vmax, dvh, lvh, svh
Conditional CSS with @supports and feature detection

quiz.question: What's the difference between dvh, svh, and lvh units?
options: dvh accounts for dynamic browser UI, svh for smallest, lvh for largest
dvh is deprecated, use svh instead
quiz.answer: dvh accounts for dynamic browser UI, svh for smallest, lvh for largest
quiz.reasoning: dvh adjusts for dynamic browser UI changes, svh is smallest viewport height, lvh is largest viewport height.

quiz.question: What does @container (min-width: 400px) and (style(--theme: dark)) query?
quiz.reasoning: Container queries can check both size (min-width) and style (--theme) conditions for adaptive components.

quiz.question: Which is better for fluid typography: clamp() or viewport units?
quiz.reasoning: clamp() provides fluid scaling with minimum and maximum boundaries, preventing extreme sizes.

days.title: Day 4 – CSS Houdini & Experimental Features
days.definition: Deep dive into CSS Houdini APIs that expose the CSS engine, allowing custom properties, paint worklets, layout algorithms, animations, and parser extensions.

explanation.main: Houdini bridges CSS and JavaScript for unprecedented styling control and performance optimization.
key_points: CSS Properties and Values API: typed custom properties with syntax validation
CSS Typed OM: JavaScript interface for typed CSS values
Paint API: programmatic canvas-based styling
Layout API: custom layout algorithms (masonry, radial, etc.)
Animation Worklet: performant, jank-free animations
Parser API: custom CSS syntax and property parsing
Font Metrics API: precise typography control

quiz.question: Which Houdini API allows creating custom CSS properties with type checking?
quiz.reasoning: Properties and Values API (CSS.registerProperty) enables typed custom properties with syntax validation.

quiz.question: What is the main performance benefit of Animation Worklet?
quiz.reasoning: Animation Worklet runs animations on the compositor thread, avoiding main thread jank.

quiz.question: Which color space is perceptual and device-independent?
quiz.reasoning: OKLCH is a perceptual color space that appears consistent across different devices and viewing conditions.

quiz.reasoning: prefers-color-scheme detects if user prefers light or dark mode, allowing theme adaptation.

quiz.question: How can CSS handle loading states without JavaScript?
options: Using data attributes with attribute selectors
quiz.answer: Using data attributes with attribute selectors

quiz.question: What's the benefit of container queries over media queries for components?
quiz.reasoning: Container queries allow components to respond to their container size, making them truly reusable across different layouts.

quiz.reasoning: prefers-reduced-motion media query respects users who prefer reduced motion due to vestibular disorders or preferences.
